title: Quota window interference between proxy and orchestrator causing tenant surge failures
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Several customers on Dedicated and Private experienced opaque 429s during tenant traffic surges. Investigation shows an intermittent mismatch between the proxy-level token-bucket window rollover and the orchestrator's quota grant reconciliation. When the proxy advanced a tenant's local credit window while the orchestrator was concurrently applying a late burst grant (from a cross-region failover or autoscale event), brief negative-credit states were generated which led to immediate rejections. The rejections propagated silently for up to 3s due to an optimization that suppresses duplicate quota refreshes. This ticket tracks the emergency fix, regression tests, rollout gating, and postmortem writeup.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Configure a Dedicated tenant with a short burst window (1s) and cross-region routing enabled
2) Drive a traffic surge from two clients that hit different frontends roughly 250-400ms apart
3) Trigger a delayed burst grant from the orchestrator (simulate autoscale or manual grant) so it applies during proxy window rollover
4) Observe per-tenant credit temporarily go negative and frontends emit 429s with opaque rejection reason
5) Reproduce is timing sensitive; use traffic replay with jitter to increase hit rate
root_cause: Race between proxy-local window advancement and orchestrator-applied grants. The proxy uses local clock-aligned windows; the orchestrator applies grants idempotently but without a canonical window leader. When a grant lands just after a proxy advanced the window, the grant was applied to the previous window, and the proxy's local subtraction for incoming tokens caused negative balances. An optimization that coalesces quota-refresh requests suppressed immediate reconciliation for ~2-3s, prolonging the outage window.
mitigation: Hotfixed proxy to: (a) accept late grants by mapping them to the current window if within grace period, (b) clamp negative balances and emit diagnostic metrics, and (c) bypass coalescing for tenants that were recently granted bursts. Also deployed an orchestrator change to tag grants with window epoch and leader id to avoid ambiguous application.
rollback_plan: If regressions observed, revert runtime PR and toggle feature flag that enables 'late-grant-mapping' on proxies. Reverting will re-enable previous behavior but keep orchestrator tagging to reduce repeat occurrences while we iterate.
comments: 2026-03-10 - Aisha Patel: Initial ticket created after escalation from Support. Customer reported spikes of 429s coincident with autoscale events. Collected logs and sample traces from two affected tenants. Attached waveform showing two frontends applying requests with ~320ms offset.

2026-03-11 - Diego Ramos: Reproduced locally in dedicated-sim using traffic-jitter harness. Confirmed negative balances appear when orchestrator burst grant lands within 100-600ms of proxy window rollover. Started prototype fix to map late grants to current window within a 750ms grace window.
2026-03-11 - Priya Nair (Reliability): Added temporary alert that fires on any tenant negative-credit > 0.5s to accelerate detection. Notified SRE on-call to watch for recurrences during rollout.

2026-03-12 - Diego Ramos: Runtime PR ready; added unit tests for window-epoch alignment and integration test that replays grant-after-rollover scenario. Running canary in us-west-2 with 5% traffic routed to patched proxies.

2026-03-12 - Support (Eliot Chen): Customers on canary tenants report normal behavior; one customer with custom gateway still saw a single 429 spike — investigating whether gateway caching masked reconciliation requests.

2026-03-13 - Diego Ramos: Orchestrator PR merged to tag grants with epoch and leader id. Canaries show reduction in opaque-429s from 0.6% to 0.02% for targeted tenants. Preparing rollout to all regions contingent on regression test pass (runtime-2.03 smoke).
2026-03-13 - Aisha Patel: Preparing postmortem template and will schedule incident review for 2026-03-18. Customer-facing summary drafted and sent to Account teams for affected tenants.

2026-03-13 - Security Review (Jamal Ortega): No customer data exfiltrated; changes limited to quota bookkeeping. Marking security_review_required = true and performing light audit of logs access in PRs.
